narrative.overview:
A quiet night in an original 16-bit action-RPG: a night-blue title with embossed gold lettering, a cave mouth opening onto a small camp, and stone-and-gold windows that hold Yeray's real CV. Warm light appears only where it matters, like a campfire in the dark: the gold of the name, the key caps, the selected tab, the chosen answer. Everything else is night, stone and crisp pixels. The interface is part of the world, not a website laid over a game, and the world invites you to sit for a while, but never makes you play: the CV is one step away from the first screen.

Density is low and deliberate: one scene, one ring of seven icons, one window at a time. Content inside the world is plain, factual and fast to scan; the game frames it and never distorts it (no invented levels, stats or percentages). Motion is stepped in whole frames, never eased; depth is bevels and hard pixel edges, never blur. Never a copy of any existing game's assets.
keyCharacteristics: Fixed 640×360 scene scaled by whole screen pixels; a UI pixel (`--u`) that grows with it.
Night palette of 32 colours; gold is the only warm accent in the interface.
Two self-hosted pixel faces: Jersey 10 for game labels, Pixelify Sans for reading.
Flat stone windows with engraved bevels, a gold-rope banner, blue selection brackets.
Stepped motion in frames; dithered fades; animations off by choice or by the system.
Characters and backgrounds are Yeray's own images, shown as they are.

rules.name: The One Warm Light Rule
rules.body: Gold is the only warm colour in the interface. If something new needs emphasis, it gets gold or nothing; never a new hue. (Red is a warning, never emphasis.)

rules.name: The Listed Pairs Rule
rules.body: Every text/background combination in use is listed in `CONTRAST_PAIRS` (`src/styles/contrast.ts`) and tested: 4.5:1 for text, 3:1 for brackets, bars and focus rings. Lowest text pair: `text-dim` on `stone-1` (the HUD's labels on the granite tile).

rules.name: The Dither Rule
rules.body: No smooth gradients. Transitions between colours are 2-colour checker dithers (sky, banner), 4×4 Bayer steps (scene fades) or hard bands (title lettering).

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: Jersey 10 speaks for the game (labels, titles, buttons); Pixelify Sans speaks for Yeray (facts to read). Never set a paragraph in Jersey 10 or a game label in Pixelify.

rules.name: The English Labels Rule
rules.body: Game labels stay English in both languages (PRESS START, SKIP INTRO, the key hints, ESC EXIT, HP, XP); the ring's names, titles, help and content are translated. The game names of the sections (ALCHEMY, EQUIP, STATS, JOURNAL, COMMS) live in the window titles, translated.

rules.name: The Zero-Blur Rule
rules.body: Every shadow has a blur of 0 and a whole-pixel offset. A soft shadow is a different era.

rules.name: The Square Pixel Rule
rules.body: If it isn't a whole number of pixels, square, it doesn't belong.

dos: Do measure every frame, gap and padding in `--u` (2–8 CSS px) and every scene position in whole scene pixels.
Do take colours only from `palette.ts` / `tokens.css` and list every new text/background pair in `CONTRAST_PAIRS`.
Do keep gold as the single warm accent (The One Warm Light Rule).

Do animate in whole frames with `steps()` or the game loop, only under `:root[data-motion='on']` or `useReducedMotion()`, and give animations off an instant equivalent that keeps the same state change.
Do keep the CV one step away: the title's parchment and the ring's CV slot (both ask, then download the PDF); keep the facts plain.
Do show Yeray's characters, icons and backgrounds exactly as he made them.
donts: Don't use border-radius, blurred shadows, transparency for shading or smooth gradients.
Don't use emoji or unicode glyphs as icons.
Don't write raw hex outside the palette files.
Don't invent stats, levels or percentages, or show the phone number on the web.
Don't copy any existing game's logo, lettering, sprites, fonts, music, names or outfits.
